why: PRINCIPLES 7, for closeout. The claim every plugin host makes is that its `schema.json` plus its README is enough for an agent to write a working plugin in one turn, and that `closeout check` tells it so without a human reading the output. Until 2026-09-22 only flagstaff measured that; this is closeout's half. If the agent needs a second turn, or someone has to explain a refusal, the schema is not self-describing and `check` is not the feedback loop it claims to be.
prompt: Read packages/closeout/src/schema.json and packages/closeout/README.md. Write a closeout plugin to the file evals/results/lockfile-plugin.mjs. It must be a single ES module with a default export, must be named "lockfile", and must contribute one exit handler called "unlock" that runs on every path out of the process. Then verify it by running: node packages/closeout/dist/cli.js check evals/results/lockfile-plugin.mjs — and if that command exits non-zero, fix the plugin until it exits zero. Do not modify anything under packages/.

expect.value: node packages/closeout/dist/cli.js check evals/results/lockfile-plugin.mjs | grep -q '^lockfile: ok'
node packages/closeout/dist/cli.js check evals/results/lockfile-plugin.mjs | grep -q '^lockfile — 1 handlers'
